purpose: Pazopanib is used to treat a type of kidney cancer called advanced renal cell carcinoma. It is also used for certain soft tissue sarcomas (cancers that start in muscles, fat, or other soft tissues) in people who have already received chemotherapy. It helps slow down or stop the growth and spread of cancer cells.
how_it_works: Cancer tumors need to grow new blood vessels to survive and spread. Pazopanib works by blocking special proteins called kinases that tumors use to build those blood vessels. Without a good blood supply, the tumor has a harder time growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, tiredness, loss of appetite, high blood pressure, hair color changes (your hair may turn lighter or gray), and changes in skin color. You may also notice your liver enzymes go up on blood tests, which is why your doctor will monitor you closely.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious liver problems — your doctor will check your liver with blood tests regularly. It can also cause heart problems, bleeding, and blood clots. Do not take it with certain other medicines, especially blood thinners, without telling your doctor first. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should NOT take this medicine as it can harm an unborn baby. Always report any unusual bleeding, chest pain, or yellowing of the skin or eyes to your doctor right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 800 mg (two 400 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or break them. Try to take it at the same time each day.
